card.title: Safety Through Nonsense
card.instruction: Take control through elaborate impossible precautions, treating every objection as another reason the people present need protection.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wear this ribbon before dinner. It prevents emotional lightning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Doubt attracts it. You'll need a second ribbon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My hands are covered. I can't hold a fork.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good catch. Metal conducts resentment. I'll feed you with a wooden spoon, after we insulate your opinions.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 imposes lightning ribbons, A3 treats disbelief as added exposure, and A5 turns disabled fork use into a reason for wood and further control of opinions.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's disbelief causes A3's second ribbon; B4's covered hands cause A5's metal-risk diagnosis and spoon-feeding offer.

relationship.evidence: B2 questions the premise and B4 points out the concrete harm caused by the precaution.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's loss of ordinary eating ability to take over feeding while expanding the protective framework.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes dinner and a supposed emotional-lightning hazard, with ribbons as the claimed protection.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's metal-conducts-resentment link is tied to B4's fork and leads to a specific wooden substitute.
